title: Look and feel, FlatLaf, and dark mode
description: How look-and-feel selection and dark mode appear in the zaproxy history: selectable look and feel in 2018, the FlatLaf dependency in 2020, the blog post that introduced dark mode as an early, rough first step, dynamic switching, and later fixes.
narrative:
For years the ZAP desktop sat under whatever look-and-feel the JVM supplied. For people who spend long stretches in that UI, dark themes had become common in the tools they used all day; a bright window during a long session is easy to find tiring.

Selection arrived first, then a proper modern set of themes. In February 2020 FlatLaf was added, bringing light and dark options into the weekly builds. A few days later a short post described the work as "first steps towards an all new dark mode for the ZAP Desktop UI" and admitted it was early: not every screen had suitable colours yet, but it was mostly usable. The post thanked @JFormDesigner for the FlatLaf look and feel that made the feature possible. Users still had to restart after changing theme.

Later that year dynamic switching removed the restart. The 2.10.0 release notes list the open-source FlatLaf themes and the two dark options among the changes. For a small open-source team, reusing a solid library rather than building one was the practical path; the work could ship in weekly builds and keep improving without blocking the main release cycle.

Theme support has continued quietly ever since. Fonts, splash screens, tree updates and SwingX panels have all been adjusted for dark look-and-feels, and FlatLaf itself is updated regularly. Dark mode is no longer an experiment; it is simply part of how ZAP looks for the people who live in it.

chapters.title: Selecting the look and feel, 2016 and 2018
chapters.text: In zaproxy, "Use L&F specified through JVM args" is dated 2016-11-02 and "Allow to select the look and feel" is dated 2018-03-01; the latter changes OptionsParamView.java and OptionsViewPanel.java.

chapters.title: FlatLaf is added, February 2020
chapters.text: On 2020-02-24 zaproxy has "Add FlatLaf L&F". Its message says it adds the FlatLaf dependency, changes ExtensionUiUtils to install the look and feel provided by FlatLaf, and is "Part of #5542 - Add a dark mode". The first release tag containing it is the weekly tag w2020-03-02. ExtensionUiUtils at HEAD lists "Flat Light", "Flat Dark", "Flat IntelliJ", and "Flat Darcula".

chapters.title: Dark mode in the weekly release
chapters.text: Two days after that weekly tag, Simon Bennetts published "Dark Mode in the Weekly Release" (2020-03-04). It announces "first steps towards an all new dark mode for the ZAP Desktop UI" and is candid about how far along it is: "It's early days - not all screens use suitable colours, but it should be mostly usable." To try it, readers open Options, choose the Display screen, select "Flat Dark" or "Flat Darcula" and restart ZAP. The post sends progress and further problems to issue 5542, the issue the FlatLaf commit says it is part of, and thanks @JFormDesigner for the FlatLaf look and feel "which adds this feature to ZAP". The commits around it fit that description of unfinished work: "Set RSyntaxTextArea dark mode is dark LookAndFeel used" is dated 2020-02-27, before the post, and "Handle dark mode in splash screen" is dated 2020-03-23, after it.

evidence.label: Dark Mode in the Weekly Release

chapters.title: Six months later: dynamic switching and ZAP 2.10.0
chapters.text: The early version needed a restart to change theme. On 2020-09-29 zaproxy has "Add support for dynamic Look and Feel switching"; its diff adds a default look and feel documented as "Flat Light" (FlatLightLaf). The release notes for 2.10.0 list "Dynamic Look and Feel including Dark Mode", say the UI includes a set of open source look and feels from FlatLaf including 2 dark mode options, and list Issue 5542, Issue 5873, and Issue 6201. The v2.10.0 tag is dated 2020-12-17.

chapters.title: Later fixes
chapters.text: Later commits in zaproxy include "fix: HTTP Panels Font setting for dark LaFs (Theme)" (2021-04-21), "Use FlatLaf add-on for SwingX" (2025-03-02, which adds one line to zap/zap.gradle.kts) and "Address UI trees not updating fully on theme switch" (2026-03-04). 58 commits in the zaproxy history have a subject beginning "Update FlatLaf".
